# Published-template source-fidelity audit, batch 11 (2026-10-23)

## Catalog and capture provenance

- The configured PostgreSQL catalog has 51 published templates. The next entries after Oltin Uzuk are Oltin Yosh, Oq Kabutar, and O‘rik Guli, each at 15,000,000 minor units (150,000 UZS). Their DB categories and supported events match the requested values: Oltin Yosh / birthday / birthday + yubiley; Oq Kabutar / wedding / wedding; O‘rik Guli / wedding / wedding + fotiha + qiz-uzatish.
- Enumerated all 13 provider `capture-manifest.json` files and searched all files under the capture root. Only `Marxaba/capture-manifest.json` lists these IDs, and all complete source folders are present: `Tug'ilgan kun va Yubiley/templates/oltin-yosh`, `Nikoh/templates/oq-kabutar`, and `Nikoh/templates/orik-guli`. The source captures were not modified.
- Oltin Yosh retains its captured body, CSS, JS, localization, metadata, and all available art, with documented local-font/shared-runtime and contract adaptations. Its captured metadata names `preview.webp`, but that file is absent from the capture. Oq Kabutar's captured body, CSS, JS, art, fonts, and opening/clothing sections are packaged; its source-only unsupported gift bank/note rows are hidden when empty. O‘rik Guli retains its captured body, source scripts, art, and localized source strings; its documented unsupported venue-photo and gift-note/bank slots remain empty/hidden. The application adapters use the same Marxaba invitation renderer for preview and public display and the centralized preview fixture only for catalog/initial selection.
- Source interactions, typed data wiring, gallery empty-state behavior, To‘yona, RSVP/wishes services, and reduced-motion branches were checked in the package notes, tests, source markup, and runtime code. The source opening interactions are present: Oltin Yosh's open button, Oq Kabutar's dove/ribbon release button, and O‘rik Guli's glass-wipe/skip controls. Reduced-motion CSS and/or JS paths remain present. No new browser session or OS reduced-motion emulation was run during the initial static pass; browser verification is recorded below.

## Confirmed catalog-art mismatches

- **Oltin Yosh:** `apps/web/public/templates/oltin-yosh/preview.webp` is a 450×800 portrait capture of the real opening, but the app locale selector is visibly baked across its top edge. The captured reference has no metadata-declared `preview.webp` to use directly. Separate cover repair task: `01a166c0-5048-71d0-b8a2-f01383585ee3`.
- **Oq Kabutar:** `apps/web/public/templates/oq-kabutar/preview.webp` shows the post-opening hero (rings, names, and floating music control). The captured first screen is a distinct closed opening with doves, ribbon, greeting, and open action. Separate cover repair task: `01a166c0-7ffb-7bb3-bb23-b365e6ea38b3`.
- **O‘rik Guli:** `apps/web/public/templates/orik-guli/preview.webp` is only the raw 780×1170 `art/view-0.webp` asset. It omits the rendered opening's window, glass-wipe control/hint, greeting, fog, petals, and bands. Separate cover repair task: `01a166c0-9433-7e23-88e3-af9f413f667c`.

Focused command `pnpm exec tsx --test tests/oltin-yosh-template.test.ts tests/oq-kabutar-localization.test.ts tests/orik-guli-template.test.ts tests/marxaba-gallery-preview.test.ts` passes 21/21. This audit made no template implementation changes, database changes, or capture edits. The three visual cover repairs are tracked separately.

## Browser verification follow-up (2026-10-23)

- Built a separate production output (`.next-b11-audit`) and opened the actual `/preview?template=<id>&qaSilent=1` routes in Chrome at 450×800. Captured initial/open screenshots for all three and repeated with both browser `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and the preview-only `qaReducedMotion=1` flag. The initial frames showed each captured opener and the full set of invitation sections; the open controls responded. Oltin Yosh and Oq Kabutar reached their post-open hero state in the normal-motion captures. O‘rik Guli's normal-motion screenshot at 3.6 seconds was still within its authored wipe/spring sequence; its reduced-motion run opened directly to the hero with no active CSS animations. The captured source itself was also opened locally to compare the initial and post-open compositions; file-URL loading emitted a missing-relative-resource warning, so those source runs are visual comparison only.
- Reduced-motion frames reported zero active CSS animations for all three. Oq Kabutar showed its source sway animation in normal mode; O‘rik Guli showed its intro/hero motion. Oltin Yosh's motion is canvas/Three.js driven, so computed CSS animation counts do not cover that behavior. There were no uncaught page errors and no HTTP error responses captured. Chrome did log a generic resource 404 once in the normal Oltin Yosh and normal O‘rik Guli runs; the correlated requests were recorded as aborted (`/templates/shared/editor-sections.js` and a Next RSC request), not as completed HTTP error responses, so no specific missing template asset was confirmed. Reduced-motion runs had no console errors.
- Production browser artifacts are in the temporary QA folder `C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp\taklifnoma-batch11-browser` (`<id>-<normal|reduced>-<initial|opened>.png`). No additional non-cover defect was confirmed. The three cover repairs remain active in their separate threads; this audit follow-up made no changes to their files.
